To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nine core personal competences rated by stakeholders as important for entering medical student success in medical school are ethical responsibility to self, and others; reliability/dependability; service orientation, social skills; capacity to improve; resilience/adaptability; cultural competence and teamwork.

the following personal competencies were rated very or extremely important to medical school success: ethical responsibility to others and self, reliability and dependability, service orientation, social skills, capacity for improvement, resilience and adaptability, cultural competence, oral communication, teamwork.

the core personal competencies identified by our research are important to entering students success in medical school and that some tools hold the promise of providing data about applicants personal competencies in a time frame that is relevant for preinterview screening.
